acceptance: Decision gate (red trunk, blocking): every poll runs the same arm-gate check as the make recipe before evaluating; if that cannot be done without duplicating the gate's logic, stop and report rather than ship a wait that evaluates the gate once. Test: waiting, then trunk turns red, ends refused and nothing is armed.
Decision gate (what counts as waiting): the wait loops only on the existing `waiting` outcome (every reason matches WAITING_MARKERS). Nothing is reclassified.

Decision gate (API budget): measure the GitHub calls of one evaluation plus one arm-gate run; choose the interval so a 60-minute wait stays under 1,000 calls, never shorter than two minutes, and record the measurement in the PR body.

Decision gate (bounds): WAIT must be a positive whole number of minutes, at most 120; anything else is refused with a usage message. Without WAIT, output and exit codes are unchanged (existing tests pass unmodified).

Decision gate (holds and refusals): a held PR (`no-auto-merge`), an unresolved thread, a failed required check, a draft PR or any other refusal ends the wait immediately as refused; one test per refusal source that the arm function already injects.

Decision gate (instruction budget): the six instruction files total at most 17,279 bytes after this PR (17,300 budget, see docs/internal/agent-instruction-evaluation.md); the AGENTS.md rewording is net zero bytes or fewer. Detail goes in docs/agent/merge-authority.md.
Decision gate (soundness): scripts/pr_arm.py and everything under make/ are soundness paths; arm only on the reviewer's success verdict for the current head.

Verification: tests/unit/scripts/test_pr_arm.py gains cases with an injected clock and sleeper, asserting the outcome line: waiting then armed arms once; waiting then refused stops polling; waiting until expiry prints the expired waiting outcome and exits 2 after the expected number of polls; no WAIT makes exactly one evaluation.

Verification (instruction eval, docs/internal/agent-instruction-evaluation.md): make agent-instructions-check, make agent-identity-check, `uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/scripts/test_agent_instruction_audit.py -q` and make skill-sync-check pass, and the printed active-byte total is not above 17,279.

Verification: `make help` shows WAIT; docs/agent/merge-authority.md states the outcome prefix, that exit 2 covers both waiting and refused, the interval and the maximum; make docs-reference-inventory-check and make pr-preflight pass.
Done when the PR is merged to develop.
context:
2026-11-11 live observation while delivering the earlier items (PR #4098, minutes after a push): `make pr-arm` printed `outcome: refused` with three reasons at once: the fast-duration verdict is missing because core has not finished (a waiting marker), `required check 'core' completed with conclusion 'failure'` (the placeholder failure from the 'CI (text edit)' run, while the real CI run was still in progress), and `review: waiting for the review's verdict`. The outcome is `waiting` only when every reason matches WAITING_MARKERS, so the usual state right after a push is `refused`. A wait that loops only on `waiting` would therefore exit at once in that state and would only help in the later window when the verdict is in and core is still running. This needs the owner's decision before building: keep the decision as made (loop only on `waiting`), or also treat a pending review verdict and a placeholder failure whose full run is in progress as waiting inside the wait loop. Ask when this item is next; it does not affect the other items.

description:
Source: a retrospective over 25 agent sessions (2026-10-18 to 2026-11-11), followed by an adversarial re-check of each claim against origin/develop 4835f5a537.

Problem. AGENTS.md says 'Check CI on a schedule, never in a loop', yet close-out needs `make pr-arm` to be repeated until the PR is armable. Sessions wrote at least 61 shell polling loops, each grepping a different string. One exited after 6 seconds on an unmatched message, one syntax error cost about an hour, and scratch watcher scripts in /tmp were lost twice. Concurrent loops may also have exhausted the GitHub API quota once (inferred, not proven).

Owner decision 2026-11-11: add `make pr-arm WAIT=<minutes>`. It polls at a fixed interval, loops only while the outcome is `waiting`, and exits at once on armed or refused. Reword AGENTS.md so this is the one allowed wait.

Change. scripts/pr_arm.py: a wait option (make variable WAIT, minutes) that re-evaluates until the outcome is not `waiting` or the time runs out; on timeout it prints `pr-arm: outcome: waiting: ... (WAIT=N expired)` and exits 2. Waiting and refused both exit 2 today; the outcome line, not the exit code, tells them apart, and this item adds no new exit code. The red-trunk gate (`scripts/trunk_revert.py arm-gate`) runs today once in the make recipe before pr_arm.py starts; in wait mode it must run again before every evaluation, with the same arguments, and a refusal from it ends the wait as refused. One fixed interval between polls, defined once, no shorter than two minutes. Durations use benchbox.utils.clock where the script may import it, otherwise time.monotonic. make/pr-landing.mk passes WAIT through; make/help.mk documents it. docs/agent/merge-authority.md documents the outcome contract (`pr-arm: outcome: waiting|refused|armed` and exit codes) and the wait. AGENTS.md 'Verification and close-out': replace 'Check CI on a schedule, never in a loop' with wording that names `make pr-arm WAIT=` as the supported wait and still forbids hand-written loops.

Evidence for the design (629 `pr-arm: outcome:` lines in the reviewed transcripts): 141 waiting, 492 refused, 66 armed. Almost all waiting lines are 'core has not finished' or the placeholder-failure wait, which this mode covers. Most refused lines are real failures (a failed core or explorer check, an open review thread, a failed gate) where polling was wasted and exiting at once is correct. About 17 were 'waiting for the review's verdict', which stays refused here.

Non-goals. No change to what arms or refuses. A pending review verdict stays `refused` and ends the wait (about 3% of observed polls; reclassifying it is the owner's call and is not part of this item). No wait mode for pr-arm-remote, pr-ready or pr-rerun. No automatic rerun, rebase, stand-in or hold change while waiting.

This item changes the close-out loop itself, so it is delivered serially and cannot be used to arm its own PR in wait mode as evidence.

Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone, and pass absolute worktree paths to every file tool; stage paths explicitly, never git add -A; no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); heavy work only via make heavy-run, never forcing admission or skipping the test lock; never bypass a required check, ruleset, hold label or review gate, and never post a stand-in; change only the files this item names, and report anything else as noticed-but-not-touched; re-read every cited file on current origin/develop before editing, because the line numbers here are hints from 2026-11-11 (origin/develop 4835f5a537); close at a merged PR (make pr-open, make pr-arm), and finish this item only after the merge is observed.
